title: The relationships the DPI-H reference architecture allows between element types
source: folio/dpi-h-ra/ch3-the-reference-architecture-for-d/t-3-3.md (Table 3.3) and t-3-2.md (Table 3.2), as reviewed in draft v1

relationships.name: Realisation
relationships.meaning: A capability is *realised* by the components and services that provide it

relationships.name: Composition
relationships.meaning: A component is *composed* of the functions and data objects it contains

relationships.name: Serving
relationships.meaning: A service *serves* the stakeholders and other elements that use it

relationships.name: Access
relationships.meaning: A component *accesses* the data objects it reads or writes

rules.note: A component realises a service it offers
A function realises the service it provides
A concrete system realises an actor (role)
An outcome signals achievement of a goal
A required service serves the component that consumes it
A service serves the stakeholders that use it
A capability serves the goal it supports
A goal is composed of sub-goals
A product bundles the services it offers
A product bundles the data it carries
A component reads/writes the data it holds
An actor performs the interaction it participates in.
A component performs its internal function
A transaction triggers the function that handles it
